issues.target: collection.name 'Red Earth, Open Sky' and calendar[11]
issues.problem: 'Red Earth' is the name of the Red Earth Festival, the long-running Native arts festival the brief itself lists as a June community moment, and 'red people' is the Choctaw root of the state name. A Nike collection branded Red Earth borrows a Native institution's name and invites a reading the brief never intended.
issues.fix: Rename the collection (for example 'Red Clay, Open Sky' or 'Clay & Sky'), keep 'Red Earth' only as a festival the team supports through paid, credited partners, and credit the Choctaw origin of 'Oklahoma' in copy only if a Choctaw partner approves it.

issues.problem: Statehood Day marks the 1907 dissolution of Indian Territory, and the re-push lands in Native American Heritage Month. The brief bans Land Run imagery but sells a celebratory 'Oklahoma' line on the anniversary of the same event, with no Native partner in the room.
issues.fix: Drop Statehood Day as a hook. Re-push the Oklahoma line on Cup Fridays or Thanksgiving week, and use November for a Native Heritage Month program built with a named nation and its artists, in a separate lane from the volume line.

issues.problem: Insight 0 says the market is Oklahoma, not OKC, and the volume line is an 'Oklahoma' wordmark. Yet the City Edition is built around an original 'Oklahoma City' script, with the state outline relegated to the jock tag. The flagship product contradicts the thesis.
issues.fix: Make the chest wordmark 'Oklahoma' (Utah and Indiana set the state-name precedent) or put the state silhouette on the court apron and shorts, and get the NBA's early read on the wordmark in the design stage.

issues.problem: Insight 1 says blue is the one color a split Sooner-and-Cowboy household shares and that browns and reds are risky. The City Edition base is rust #A8442A, a non-blue jersey sitting between OU crimson, OSU orange and Texas burnt orange, with Thunder blue demoted to accent. The brief's own risk list flags this problem and then ships it.
issues.fix: Flip the hierarchy: Dark Blue or Thunder Blue body with rust as horizon, yoke and number-keyline, or test the rust base in OKC and Tulsa fan panels against OU and OSU gear before committing. The jersey should still pass the blue-peace-treaty test.

issues.problem: Today is Oct 9. Plaza Walls and the State Fair (September) have already happened, so the Red Dirt preview is impossible. A launch the week of Oct 12 for a new Storm-front gradient capsule and a Red Dirt capsule with a commissioned poster artist needs an NBA-licensed, tooled-and-dyed line, which takes months, not days.
issues.fix: Say which items already exist in the Fall 2026 line and re-skin only those for Oct 20. Move the Red Dirt capsule and the poster-artist commission to a Spring 2027 launch (April with Festival of the Arts) and a September 2027 Plaza Walls preview.

issues.problem: 405 is the OKC metro area code; Tulsa is 918 and western Oklahoma is 580. A '405 state-outline hoodie' pushed hardest into Tulsa and small-town doors tells those buyers the product is for Oklahoma City, which undercuts the 'one-team state' idea, and the culture dossier notes Tulsa as the in-state rival city.
issues.fix: Use the state outline alone for the statewide layer, and make 405 an OKC-metro tee. Make a 918 Tulsa tee and a 580 tee for the west and south as a set, each aimed at a different door.

issues.target: partners, risks and opportunities[5], gym-pride (Tulsa and Booker T. Washington)
issues.problem: Tulsa is the second hub, with a Brookside pop-up and a Booker T. Washington gym program, but Greenwood, Black Wall Street and the 1921 massacre appear nowhere in the risks. The art dossier flags that memorial and Black Wall Street imagery belongs to local Black artists. A brand pop-up near that history, with no Tulsa-based Black partner named, is an avoidable error.
issues.fix: Add a risk line: no Greenwood, Black Wall Street or massacre imagery and no activation dates near May 31 or Juneteenth without a named Tulsa Black partner. Name a Tulsa-based partner for the Booker T. Washington gym program and confirm what the school wants before any Thunder branding goes in.

issues.problem: The brief treats the First Americans Museum as a broker for a 'nation-authored' edition. The museum is a civic institution for 39 sovereign nations and cannot speak for any of them, and the brief names no nation, no Native artist working in apparel and no pay structure beyond 'credit and pay'. Yatika Starr Fields is Cherokee, Osage and Muscogee, so one person could be treated as stand-in for three nations.
issues.fix: Use the museum only for introductions, then go to the tribal commerce or cultural offices of the nations involved. Name the nation first, set the commission terms and approval rights in writing, and treat Fields as an individual artist with his own commission rather than a representative.

issues.target: calendar and missed signals (Native Heritage Month, Nike N7)
issues.problem: Oklahoma has 39 federally recognized nations and some of the biggest tribal-owned businesses in the market, yet the brief has no November Native Heritage Month plan and ignores Nike's existing N7 program, which is the established, credentialed route for Indigenous-led product and giving. Nations that sponsor sports are also the obvious statewide co-investor.
issues.fix: Add a Nov calendar slot that uses the N7 pathway and its Native design partners, with a named OKC-based nation or Native-owned designer as lead and Thunder-side partners confirmed. Check which nations already hold Thunder sponsorships before approaching any.

issues.problem: Storm gradients, sunset skies and wind lines pass the swap test for Kansas City, Dallas or Denver, and the Thunder's own blue-orange-yellow palette is already a sunset. The brief also lists the gradient as the signature texture without knowing whether a past City Edition or the 2008 identity used it, as its own verify list admits.
issues.fix: Anchor the sky in something only Oklahoma has: the Skydance Bridge sail line already in the brief, the flat sky-blue field of the state flag, or Tulsa and OKC Deco rooflines against a storm. Check the earlier Thunder City Editions before using the gradient as a headline idea.

issues.problem: Pearl snaps, canvas, tooled leather and boot-cut denim also describe Fort Worth, Houston, Calgary and Cheyenne, and Red Dirt music is a Texas scene as much as an Oklahoma one. The capsule's audience is the Okie-pride crowd, while the brief cites no evidence that Thunder buyers want a Nike western line, and the NBA's growing Black and international fan base is barely addressed.
issues.fix: Cut to what is Oklahoma: Stillwater, Cain's Ballroom-style gig-poster lettering, Turnpike Troubadours or John Moreland shows booked by a Red Dirt venue, and Stockyards City stores like Langston's. Keep the capsule at priority 2 and pair it with a hoops-first line to avoid presenting the Thunder as a country team.

issues.problem: The Southside lowrider candy-paint release has a colour (#4B3FA0) and a story but no named partner, no car club or painter, no calendar moment and no month in the District Series rollout. It reads as a cue lifted from a community without a plan, which is the exact pattern the brief says it avoids.
issues.fix: Either name a Southside partner (a car club, painter or Capitol Hill business) and a community moment such as Cinco de Mayo in Capitol Hill or Hispanic Heritage Month, or drop the release. Do not use candy-paint violet until a credited painter is attached.

issues.problem: The Asian District anchor is a chef (Jeff Chanchaleune), not a visual artist, and the brief says only 'a Vietnamese or Lao OKC artist'. Lunar New Year 2027 is Feb 6, only four months out, which is too short for artist selection, contracts, NBA licensing sign-off and production. Vietnamese, Chinese, Korean and Lao communities each have distinct events and the brief collapses them.
issues.fix: Move the first release to Festival of the Arts or Paseo in spring 2027, and treat Lunar New Year 2028 as the Asian District date. Use the chef for introductions and a food pairing, and recruit the designer through the Asian District business association and Oklahoma Contemporary.

issues.target: opportunities[1] (Loud City playoff fast-turn) and retailPlaybook
issues.problem: Series-win and conference-round graphics are typically controlled by the NBA and Fanatics, so a 48-hour turn into Academy, Dick's and Hibbett statewide is unrealistic for a Nike-led program. Ship-to-store for rural doors also adds days, and the Nike Factory Store carries overruns rather than launch product.
issues.fix: Scope the fast-turn to Nike.com, the arena store and one or two metro doors, and coordinate graphics with the league's playoff licensing calendar. Remove the Factory Store from launch channels and use it for sell-through of the under-$100 line.

issues.problem: 'Unfinished business' after a playoff loss fits the Spurs, Nuggets or any contender, and the copy asks fans to wear a loss. The brief's 'earned, defiant champion details' is unclear now that the Knicks are the reigning champions and the Thunder's title is 2025.
issues.fix: Make the hook Thunder-specific: the Presti-built draft-and-develop core, the Mara and Williams development story and 'Loud City' at Paycom Center. Keep any 2025 champion reference to licensed commemorative marks only.

issues.problem: The brief leads with an 'SGA name-and-number tee' but ignores that SGA, a two-time MVP and Hamilton-born tunnel-fit regular, is a major style story. His shoe deal sits with Converse, a Nike-owned sister brand, so player product needs coordination, and name-and-number items run through NBPA group licensing.
issues.fix: Add a tunnel-fit and Canadian-fan angle, confirm which brand and licensing path covers SGA, Williams and Holmgren product, and keep the player tees to licensed formats Nike can actually ship.

issues.problem: The music dossier surfaces The Flaming Lips, OKC's psychedelic alt-rock institution, and the Red Dirt songwriters, but the partner list has no musician and no venue except a passing Jones Assembly mention. Hip-hop is only represented by Jabee.
issues.fix: Add one music partner on each side (a Red Dirt booker and an OKC hip-hop or alt-rock voice) and use their posters and stage lettering as the artist layer, which also makes the gig-poster tee less of a design-team invention.

issues.problem: Okemah is a very small town hosting a folk festival, and the calendar links it to a shooting shirt and an Oklahoma wordmark tee with no explanation of why festival-goers would buy either. It also invites using Guthrie's catalog and name, which are separately rights-controlled.
issues.fix: Replace with a real summer retail beat such as the NBA Draft, Summer League or the August tax-free stock-in, and treat Guthrie as inspiration only unless the estate is licensed.

strengths: The 'market is Oklahoma, not OKC' thesis is the most specific idea in the brief, and the Tulsa allocation, small-town Academy and Hibbett doors, and August under-$100 tax holiday are grounded in real retail behavior no other NBA market shares.
The blue-led, split-Sooner-and-Cowboy-household rule is a sharp, usable design constraint with hex values, and the brief mostly respects it outside the City Edition.
The avoid lists are strong: no Native regalia or Osage shield, no memorial, bombing or tornado-damage imagery, no Land Run or oil-derrick kitsch, no Sonics colors, no crimson-leaning reds.

Named partners (Plaza District Association, Jabee, Oklahoma Contemporary, Factory Obscura, Shop Good) are real, local and appropriate, and the credit, pay and community-launch rule for every community-sourced piece is the right standard.

Palette hex values match the Thunder's published Dark Blue, Thunder Blue, Sunset and Yellow, and the calendar correctly pins the Oct 20 San Antonio opener, Oct 22 Denver game, Cup Fridays and Christmas at Minnesota.
summary: A strong, locally grounded strategy whose statewide-value thesis is its best idea, but the flagship pieces undercut it: a rust-based 'Oklahoma City' jersey contradicts the blue-peace-treaty, Oklahoma-not-OKC thesis, and the 'Red Earth' collection name and Statehood Day push risk real appropriation missteps with Native partners. Several September and mid-October launches are already past or unrealistic, the 405 tag misfires in Tulsa, and Tulsa's Greenwood history and Nike N7 are missing. Fix the naming, target-season and Tulsa risks first; the rest is sharpening. Confidence is medium because it rests on model knowledge, not a live check.
